title: Triggered eval signal hub for pinned models and config changes
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build a centralized "triggered eval signal hub" that converts model version pin/upgrade and config changes (catalog and tenant-pinned) into prioritized eval jobs and alertable quality checks. Background: We've relied on ad-hoc hooks for pin events; coverage is inconsistent between catalog upgrades and customer-specific pins. This ticket proposes a single event-to-eval orchestration layer that enforces sampling, priority, and fallbacks, and emits standardized metadata for downstream eval runners and dashboards. Scope: 1) Event ingestion: webhook + internal event stream handlers for model pin, model catalog publish, config diff on inference routes. 2) Signal enrichment: attach customer tier, recent production traffic patterns, last-known eval fingerprint, and pinned artifact metadata. 3) Prioritization rules: high-priority for enterprise tenants and catalog-major upgrades, medium for regular catalog minor patches, low for non-production pins. 4) Eval job generation: map signals to eval job templates (smoke, fidelity, safety) with sampling parameters. 5) Backpressure & throttling: global rate cap and tenant-level limits; queue spillover goes to lightweight smoke evals. 6) Observability: event audit trail, queue metrics, job success/failure, latency to first result, and a rejection reason taxonomy. 7) Integrations: notify Console rollouts, create alert hooks in PagerDuty if fidelity regressed to >10% of baseline. Out-of-scope: building new eval suites; this ticket only orchestrates and triggers existing eval runners.
acceptance_criteria: Event hub receives model pin and catalog publish events and logs them to audit stream within 1 minute of occurrence.
Signals enriched with customer tier, pinned-version hash, and last-production-traffic snapshot for >95% of events.
Eval jobs created follow prioritization rules and are enqueued in eval-runner FIFO queue with correct template parameters.
System enforces global rate limit and tenant caps; when capped, a lightweight smoke eval is created instead of full fidelity by default.
Console shows per-event trace link, job id, and status; at least one automated alert triggers for a simulated regression test in staging.
Documentation and runbook for oncall with clear failure modes and remediation steps added to Confluence.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): ingest events and produce enriched audit logs, no evals run (2 days). Phase 2 (canary customers): enable eval generation for 3 low-traffic tenants and run smoke evals only (1 week). Phase 3 (catalog canary): enable for catalog minor upgrades for internal catalog models with medium fidelity evals (2 weeks). Phase 4 (gradual increase): lift tenant caps and enable enterprise priority paths; monitor SLOs before full production.
metrics: percent_events_throttled <= 5% (target), with fallback smoke evals emitted
test_plan: Unit tests for event parsing and enrichment. Integration tests that inject synthetic pin events into staging and assert correct job templates created. Chaos test: simulate eval-runner queue saturation and confirm fallback smoke evals are created and logged. End-to-end manual verification checklist for canary tenants and catalog canary with sample dataset and baseline metrics.
notes: Trade-offs: centralizing logic simplifies consistency but creates a single coordination point that needs high availability and retry/backoff semantics.
Decision: use existing eval-runner job schema to avoid duplicate work; extend schema with `source_event_id` and `priority_score` fields.
Privacy: event payloads exclude raw user content; only metadata and small traffic summaries are attached to signals.
Risk: aggressive sampling on a large catalog publish could overload eval runners; mitigated by rate limiting and prioritized queuing.
